properties.decision:
**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-08-28.

📌 The near-match offered was `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed`, and it is the right one to have offered — but it is a different act. That RULE says what should happen. This asks whether reflow2 should SERVE a method for doing it, and whether a method is even the missing piece.

═══ HIS IDEA, IN HIS WORDS ═══

A `/rca` skill: *"my implemented design experienced problem X"* → the skill walks the design systematically and returns POSSIBLE root causes. Useful when testing an implemented design, and after something has been fielded and fails.

He gave the method: define the problem with measurable specifics; collect data; identify causal factors; find the root cause past the obvious trigger; implement and monitor corrective action. Principles: causes not symptoms, evidence not assumption, blameless, structured, prevent recurrence.

⭐ **AND HE GAVE THE MOTIVATION, WHICH IS THE SHARPEST PART:** *"quite a few cases now where in using reflow2 on a project, the agent proposes a solution to an issue, then goes off and implements some solution, but it turns out that the solution only treated a symptom or superficial issue and not the root cause... basically, trying to stem the agent's tendency to be over-confident in identifying an issue without doing proper RCA."*

═══ 🛑 TWO THINGS ALREADY IN THE DESIGN THAT CHANGE THE QUESTION ═══

**① THE METHOD ALREADY EXISTS AND IS HIS.** `rule:an-issue-is-root-caused-then-pinned-by-a-test-then-fixed` — Anthony, 2026-08-26 — carries the ordered method: root-cause it, pin it with a test that FAILS TODAY, fix at the cause, test, write the cause down. It is `enforced: false` by his own decision, and its own text states the cost: *"advisory rules get skipped, and this rule exists precisely because F-01's own fix skipped step ②."* **So the method is not missing. It is written, it is his, and it is not being followed.** A skill that restates it produces a second copy of an instruction already being skipped, and looks like progress while doing it.

**② THE MEASURED FAILURE WAS SURFACING, NOT METHOD.** `fact:the-root-cause-was-on-the-record-and-a-session-re-derived-it-anyway` (2026-08-22) is the one to read before choosing. A root cause was ALREADY written down, findable by the error string. Three days later a session hit the same error twice, diagnosed it from scratch, and wrote *"second occurrence, so it is a reliable pattern"* into its handoff — while a node saying *"nine occurrences, here is the cause, here is the fix"* sat in the graph. Its conclusion: ***"The gap is not accumulation, it is SURFACING — nothing puts a known root cause in front of the session at the moment it hits the symptom."***

⚠️ **A SKILL IS A METHOD, AND A SKILL HAS TO BE REACHED FOR** — which is the exact failure above. This does not kill the idea. It means option (a) alone probably does not reach what he is aiming at.

═══ MEASURED 2026-08-28, so the options are costed against fact rather than guess ═══

**The causal vocabulary EXISTS AND IS ALREADY IN USE** — nothing here needs a schema change: `CAUSES` 26, `TRIGGERS` 9, `MITIGATES` 14, `RISKS` 11, `BLOCKS` 11, `CONTRADICTS` 53, `INVALIDATES` 15.

**There is a corpus of repairs to reason over:** of 703 ChangeEvents, 103 are `test_failure_fix` and 60 are `defect_fix` — 163 fixes. `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` (ACCEPTED, unbuilt) asks each to say whether it reached the cause; none does yet.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══

**(a) A SERVED SKILL, like the other twenty.** Walks the graph from the symptom: which capability is implicated, which artifacts realize it, which ChangeEvents touched them, which TemporalFacts already describe them, what verification covers them. Returns CANDIDATE causes with the evidence for each. Cheapest, consistent with the rest of the surface, no schema change. ⚠️ Counter: it has to be reached for, and ② is the measured proof that reaching is the failing step.

**(b) MAKE THE RCA WRITE CAUSAL STRUCTURE.** The output is not prose but `CAUSES` / `TRIGGERS` edges from symptom to cause, so the NEXT occurrence finds the prior analysis by search. ⭐ This is what turns one investigation into a permanent answer, and the vocabulary is already there and in use. ⚠️ Counter: does nothing for a first occurrence, and pays off only if somebody searches — which is ② again.

**(c) SURFACE A KNOWN CAUSE AT THE MOMENT OF THE SYMPTOM.** What ② says is actually missing: something that, when a session hits or reports a symptom, puts the already-recorded cause in front of it unasked. ⚠️ Counter: needs a trigger, and reflow2 has no hook into "the agent just saw an error" — though SessionStart and Stop hooks prove the harness CAN be reached. Most valuable, least specified, nobody has costed it.

**(d) A DETECTOR ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN ON THE AGENT.** Build the accepted-and-unbuilt `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` and let the design answer "how much of this stands on a patch?". ⚠️ Counter: post-hoc — it catches the shallow fix after it ships, which is better than nothing and is not what he asked for.

**(e) ENFORCE THE EXISTING RULE INSTEAD OF ADDING ANYTHING.** ⚠️ Counter, and it is already settled once: the rule's own text explains why it is advisory — nothing in a diff or a CI run can see whether a test was FAILING before the fix, so an enforced version could only check something weaker, and *"a check that reads as enforcement while measuring something else is worse than no check."* Reopening needs an argument that text does not already answer.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT SHOULD BE CHECKED BEFORE CHOOSING ═══

1. **Is the target the AGENT or the RECORD?** He said "stem the agent's tendency", which is (a)/(c). The graph can only reach the record, which is (b)/(d). Different products; the wording does not settle which.
2. **How many of the 163 recorded fixes actually treated a symptom?** UNMEASURED. He says "quite a few cases now" and nothing counts them — the same unmeasured-n trap `dec:idea-what-makes-a-field-report-owed` was designed against, where the 2026-08-28 sweep found the raw count and the real one differed by a factor of forty.
3. **Would this have caught the two instances from the session it was proposed in?** Both are live. A recorded diagnosis whose REASONING had gone stale while its conclusion stayed true; and an agent reading a fact about a RETIRED dependency as though it described this project. **Both were caught by measuring, not by method** — which is evidence about what actually works here.
4. **`dec:idea-which-agent-pitfalls-can-reflow2-actually-reach` is the parent question**, and is the highest-ranked open decision in the design. Overconfident diagnosis is precisely an agent failure mode; whether reflow2 can reach it belongs there, not here.
properties.name: DECIDED — reflow2 serves an RCA method, and the design GENERATES the candidates: option (a) with (b) folded in as its step ⑧
properties.rationale:
SETTLED BY ANTHONY, 2026-08-28, across three messages that each corrected the framing — which is why the options above are left standing rather than trimmed.

① HE NARROWED THE TARGET: *"not so much can the graph help determine root cause... it is more to direct the agent how to properly do the steps of root cause analysis and not just jump to quick solutions."* That answers must-check question 1 — AGENT, not RECORD — which had been answered by assumption while option (c) was being costed in detail.

② THEN HE WIDENED IT BACK, and this is the correction that made the result worth shipping: *"you can often start fishbone analysis on inspecting the design... there is value in looking at a design (and if it is a software code base that is being implemented in a reflow2 project, then you can inspect the implementation of the design also)."* The first draft had over-corrected into pure process guidance whose step ③ read "write down at least three candidate causes" — an exhortation that yields two real candidates and a filler written to satisfy the instruction. Step ③ now walks NINE BONES, each answered by a call, with the artifact layer as the bridge from symptom to source files.

③ *"let's get to work implementing it."*

═══ WHAT WAS CHOSEN ═══

**(a) A SERVED SKILL — taken**, and its answer to (a)'s own counter ("it has to be reached for") is that a rule read once at handshake and a skill pulled at the moment of the work fail differently. The rule was not enough; that is the evidence, not a hope.

**(b) WRITE CAUSAL STRUCTURE — taken, folded in as step ⑧** rather than built separately: the skill requires a `CAUSES` edge from cause to symptom, because the repair is recoverable from the diff and the cause is not.

**(c) SURFACE AT THE MOMENT OF THE SYMPTOM — NOT taken, and now costed.** `fact:surfacing-a-known-cause-is-cheap-and-reaches-the-wrong-half` holds the measurement. It triggers on a FAILING TOOL CALL, and an overconfident fix compiles, passes and ships green — so it reaches the recurring-known-error case and not the case that prompted this. ⚠️ ITS COSTING ALSO CONTAINED THREE WRONG DIAGNOSES, corrected only by a discriminating test: the real cost is a one-time per-MCP-session hydrate (41.11s, then 0.05s), so a hook — a fresh process every time — pays it on every call. Inline is impossible, which is why `graph_probe.py` is detached. The option remains open on its own merits and is a different product.

**(d) A DETECTOR ON THE RECORD — NOT taken, and it is the honest next increment.** `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` is ACCEPTED and unbuilt. The skill supplies the INSTRUCTION and step ⑧ supplies the write; nothing yet NOTICES when a fix lands with no cause recorded. By this project's own three-legs finding that is two legs of three.

**(e) ENFORCE THE RULE INSTEAD — NOT taken**, and its counter stands unchanged: nothing in a diff or a CI run can see whether a test was failing before the fix, so an enforced version could only measure something weaker, and a check that reads as enforcement while measuring something else is worse than no check.
